title: Match a leader arm to its follower before enabling teleoperation, then steer the follower round a glass onto a dot
instruction: Use the yellow leader arm to put the black follower arm's tip on the green dot. Press ENABLE to start teleoperation: from then on, the follower copies the leader's joint angles.
context: Many robot-learning demonstrations are recorded on leader-follower rigs (ALOHA, GELLO, SO-101 leader arms), where the follower tracks the leader's joint positions: if the two differ when tracking starts, the follower jumps at once to close the gap. Operators pose the leader to match the follower before engaging, and some rig software refuses to engage while the gap is large. Surgical master-slave robots and bumpless manual-to-automatic transfer in process control follow the same rule.
setup: Station table; positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. Angles are seen from above, counter-clockwise positive: a shoulder angle is link 1's direction (base axis to elbow axis) measured from +x (straight away from the robot); an elbow angle is the turn from link 1's direction to link 2's (elbow axis to tip axis). Both arms are two-link arms on vertical joint axes with identical bases mounted the same way round, so equal angles give the same shape. (1) Follower arm (black), base axis fixed at (55, 0), beyond the robot's reach: a 7 cm black aluminium column 5 cm tall on a flange; black anodised aluminium links 2.8 cm wide and 1.6 cm thick, stacked 5 to 8.2 cm high, link 1 14 cm between axes (250 g), link 2 16 cm (200 g); at the tip a 3 cm silver end cap over a 1.2 cm steel pointer that ends 5 mm above the board. Shoulder -135 to +110 deg, elbow 0 to 150 deg (it bends counter-clockwise only). Its joints have stiff position motors; while teleoperation is off they hold. Start: shoulder -56, elbow +30, tip at (77.2, -18.6). (2) Follower board: light grey HDPE, 41 x 56 cm, 6 mm thick, x 49 to 90, y -28 to 28, fixed. (3) Glass: a blue-tinted glass tumbler, 7.4 cm across, 10 cm tall, 250 g, standing loose on the board with its base centred at (79.3, 3.4). (4) Green dot: a green vinyl circle 5 cm across on the board, centred at (77.2, 18.6), where the follower's tip is at shoulder +24, elbow +30. (5) Leader arm (yellow), a 0.75-scale replica of the follower, base axis fixed at (24, 26): a black servo column 5 cm across and 2 cm tall; yellow PLA links 2.1 cm wide and 1.2 cm thick, 10.5 and 12 cm between axes, about 30 g each, a black servo body at the elbow; a black ribbed rubber knob 2.5 cm across and 5 cm tall on a free-turning bearing over link 2's end, its top 9.4 cm high. Same joint ranges as the follower; its joints have friction, so it stays where it is left. Start: shoulder +64, elbow +140 (folded), knob at (17.6, 30.6). (6) Leader mat: black rubber, 32 x 36 cm, 3 mm thick, centred at (28, 27), fixed. (7) ENABLE box: black ABS enclosure, 8 x 8 x 4.5 cm, centred at (22, -8), fixed. On its lid, 1 cm beyond its centre, a 30 mm blue illuminated push button stands 8 mm proud in a silver bezel, sprung, with 6 mm of travel; a white ENABLE label is printed on the lid's near half. Teleoperation starts the first time the button is pushed down 4 mm and then stays on: the button lights, and every control step the follower's shoulder and elbow are driven toward the leader's angles at up to 3 rad/s each. (8) Two grey 6 mm cables lie on the table from each arm's base to the ENABLE box. object_jitter 0.
scoring: Angles as in the setup. Gap: the larger of the shoulder difference and the elbow difference between leader and follower, in degrees. Enable: the first moment the ENABLE button is pushed down 4 mm or more; teleoperation then stays on for the rest of the trial, and pressing it again does nothing. Clean enable: the gap at the enable is 15 deg or less. Glass disturbed: the centre of its base moves more than 1 cm from where it started, or it tilts more than 10 deg from upright. On the dot: the axis of the follower's tip pointer is within 2 cm, horizontally, of the dot's centre. 0 at any moment, for the rest of the trial: the glass is disturbed, by anything; or the enable is not clean (a gap over 15 deg, so the follower jumps to the leader at full speed). Otherwise: 1.0 (success, ends the trial) for a clean enable and then the follower's tip staying on the dot for 1 s; at the run limit, 0.5 after a clean enable when the tip is not on the dot or has not stayed there for 1 s, and 0 if ENABLE was never pressed. Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 1.0. Examples: pressing ENABLE first, or posing the leader at the dot's pose and then pressing ENABLE, scores 0 (the follower sweeps through the glass); matching, enabling and dragging the knob straight to the goal takes the follower's outer link through the glass and scores 0; matching within 15 deg, enabling and stopping scores 0.5. The robot may grip, push or release the leader any number of times; its arms are not scored. Real trial: an overhead video; angles with a protractor on the frame where the ENABLE lamp lights; distances with a ruler.
reset_notes: With teleoperation off, return the follower to shoulder -56, elbow +30, fold the leader to shoulder +64, elbow +140, and stand the glass back on its spot.
fidelity: 240 Hz GPU physics, 20 Hz control. The follower is a fixed-base articulation on stiff position drives (12 N m cap); each control step its targets move toward the leader's angles at up to 3 rad/s, one step behind. The leader's joint friction is stick-slip (a weak spring to a set point that follows each joint with 0.3 deg of play) with damping, so it stays where left. The button is a sprung sliding joint; its lamp is a swapped cap. Cables are visual only. Real trials use a plastic tumbler.
